fromContent: In the Vornic protocol, only anchor nodes reset a packet's drift counter to zero; ordinary relays only increment it.
toContent: To cross a wide Vornic region without being dropped, a packet must be routed through at least one anchor node along the way.
note: native depends: from=premise, to=conclusion that depends on it

fromContent: Glimmer-moth larvae feed exclusively on the saber fern and can eat no other plant.
toContent: A program to save the glimmer moth from extinction must begin by protecting and replanting saber-fern groves.

fromContent: Every function in the Korl language is pure: its result is determined solely by its arguments, with no side effects.
toContent: A Korl compiler may cache and reuse the result of any function call it has already evaluated, with no risk of a stale answer.

fromContent: An unspent tithe-credit loses ten percent of its value at the end of each cycle.
toContent: Prudent tithe-credit holders convert their balances into durable goods before each cycle closes.

fromContent: In Castellan, the keep may never move onto a tile that an enemy warden threatens.
toContent: A player can pen the enemy keep into a corner by posting two wardens to cover all of its escape tiles.

fromContent: The sap of a lumen tree conducts electricity readily.
toContent: Experienced foresters never shelter beneath a lumen tree during a thunderstorm.

fromContent: Every Daftari write operation auto-commits to git.
toContent: A user can recover any earlier state of a Daftari vault using ordinary git commands.

fromContent: A Vornic relay discards any packet whose accumulated drift exceeds the relay's tolerance.
toContent: When a previously reliable Vornic route suddenly starts losing packets, it is a sign the path has grown longer than the drift limit allows.

fromContent: Korl evaluates every expression lazily, computing a value only at the moment some later step demands it.
toContent: A Korl programmer can define a stream in terms of itself to build an infinite self-referential sequence that still runs.

fromContent: Glimmer moths steer their flight solely by the polarization pattern of moonlight.
toContent: Researchers can herd and track glimmer moths by setting out artificial polarized-light beacons.

fromContent: Every merchant in the realm must accept tithe-credits at their full face value.
toContent: A traveler carrying tithe-credits can always buy goods at any market stall without bargaining over whether the credits will be taken.

fromContent: Daftari's write locks expire automatically after a 60-second time-to-live.
toContent: A Daftari vault left locked by a crashed agent becomes writable again on its own within a minute, with no manual cleanup.
